Limited loss does not mean low risk: losing the full premium is a common outcome for short-dated, out-of-the-money options."}, {"source": "black-scholes-limits#1", "relevance": 0.67, "text": "Limits of the Black-Scholes model | Assumptions: Black-Scholes assumes European exercise (only at expiration), constant volatility, continuous trading and no dividends unless adjusted for. Real markets break these assumptions, especially around events and in thinly traded contracts."}, {"source": "vega#2", "relevance": 0.66, "text": "Vega | Why vega matters around events: Longer-dated options have more vega than short-dated ones. Before events such as earnings, a long option's value depends heavily on IV, so a post-event drop in IV can erase gains from the stock's move. Multiplying vega by the expected IV drop gives a quick estimate of the loss from volatility crush."}]}
